root_cause.hypothesis: App-side connection/transaction leak: code path issuing SELECT count(*) FROM warden_proving_ground opens transaction but never commits/rolls back or returns connection to pool, leaving idle-in-transaction sessions to accumulate. Not a deploy regression (empty deploy list) and not lock contention or connection exhaustion (locks_waiting=0, usage only 25%) — early-stage leak, not yet critical.
evidence: 10 pids idle_in_transaction 359-363s, all same query text — same code path repeatedly leaking
long_running_queries=0 — query itself completes fast, transaction just never closes
locks_waiting=0 — no blocking contention yet, consistent with early/slow leak
connections_used_pct=0.25 — not yet connection-pool exhaustion, but trending toward it
RECENT DEPLOYS empty — rules out a bad release as trigger
ruled_out: Slow/expensive query causing pileup (long_running_queries=0, query is a simple count)
Connection pool exhaustion as root cause (usage only 25%, though risk if trend continues)

proposal.target: warden prod postgres: idle-in-transaction sessions running SELECT count(*) FROM warden_proving_ground (pids 3615,3616,3618,3619,3620,3621,3624,3629,3630,3632)
proposal.reasoning: 10 idle-in-transaction sessions stuck 359-363s on same query, no locks waiting, usage only 25%, no deploy correlation. App-side leak not committing/rolling back. Killing stuck backends frees them immediately; underlying leak still needs code fix.
proposal.expected_effect: Stuck backends terminated, connections returned to pool, idle_in_transaction count drops to ~0. Does not fix root cause — leak will recur until app code patched.
